source_caption:
🎬 Trust (1990)

Trust follows Maria Coughlin, a rebellious and outspoken teenager whose life takes an unexpected turn after a heated argument with her family leads to devastating consequences. Suddenly pregnant, rejected by her boyfriend, and forced to confront an uncertain future, Maria finds herself struggling to survive in a world where nearly everyone seems determined to judge or control her. Her circumstances begin to change when she meets Matthew Slaughter, an intelligent but emotionally troubled young man who has grown increasingly frustrated with society, his family, and the expectations placed upon him. Despite their contrasting personalities and complicated personal histories, Maria and Matthew develop an unusual connection built on honesty, curiosity, and a shared sense of alienation. As their friendship gradually evolves into romance, they begin questioning traditional ideas about relationships, responsibility, independence, and what it means to build a meaningful life. However, their growing bond faces challenges from family tensions, financial difficulties, personal insecurities, and the consequences of their decisions. Through awkward encounters, dark humor, emotional conversations, and unexpected moments of tenderness, both characters discover that genuine trust requires vulnerability and understanding. Combining unconventional romance, sharp dialogue, memorable performances, and thought-provoking storytelling, Trust explores love, loneliness, identity, family conflict, personal responsibility, and the difficult journey toward emotional maturity.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Drama • Romance

⭐ IMDb: 7.3/10

⏱️ Runtime: 1h 47m • R

🎥 Director: Hal Hartley

✍️ Writer: Hal Hartley

source_details.synopsis: Trust is a 1990 romantic black comedy film written and directed by Hal Hartley and starring Adrienne Shelly, Martin Donovan, Merritt Nelson, Edie Falco, and John MacKay. In the film, two young misfits with a troubled home life meet by chance in a Long Island town and through trials develop a platonic relationship based on mutual respect, admiration, and trust.
